payload.title: The infrastructure-policy adapter walks every file classifyInfraFile owns under the seven new roots, but the manifest grants only Dockerfile and compose globs there, so a classified terraform, nginx, nats, k8s, helm or override file is dropped by the kernel snapshot with no observation or claim
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/infrastructure-policy-adapter.ts:390-403 (the walk includes every file classifyInfraFile returns non-null for, then filterFilesBySnapshot)
tools/aria-adapters/adapter-fs.ts:270-280 (a file absent from repo_snapshot.allowed_paths is filtered out with no trace)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/tool_runner.py:380-389 (the kernel narrows allowed_paths to the manifest's allowed_read_globs before the adapter runs)
tools/aria-adapters/infrastructure-policy-adapter.tool.json:92-112 (each new root grants only Dockerfile*, *.{Dockerfile,dockerfile} and {docker-,}compose*.{yml,yaml})
tools/gates/lib/infra/classify.ts:51-86 (the classifier also owns .tf/.tfvars, .tpl, nginx and nats .conf, k8s and helm yaml, kustomization and *.override.yml)
tools/aria-adapters/infrastructure-policy-adapter.test.ts:1418-1433 (the only guard is a test over tracked files)
payload.rule_violated: Adapter header 'No silent skip' (infrastructure-policy-adapter.ts:39) and the single-owner rule: what the adapter walks (classifyInfraFile) and what the manifest reads (hand-listed globs) are two definitions of one surface.
payload.notes: Reproduced with the revision's classifier and the kernel's own find_scope_violations against the manifest: apps/x/values.yaml, libs/x/main.tf, web/x/nginx.conf, apps/x/kustomization.yaml, apps/x/nats/nats.conf, apps/x/chart/templates/a.tpl, apps/x/k8s/deploy.yaml and apps/x/foo.override.yml are all classified infrastructure files yet fall outside the manifest read scope (docker-compose.override.yml and Dockerfile are inside). In a kernel run the snapshot omits them, the adapter's walk collects them and the filter drops them before any observation, so a privileged compose override, an unpinned terraform module or a header-dropping nginx level under apps, libs, web, platform, e2e, sens-api-gateway or scripts is never judged and nothing says so. 211 tracked files are classified under the roots today and none falls outside the scope, so the surface is latent; the only guard is the tracked-file test, which is not triggered by these files (see the cache-inputs finding). Close condition: Make the adapter's walk under the new roots use the manifest's own read scope (one owner), or emit an observation for each classified file the snapshot omits; prove it with a test that places a .tf, an nginx.conf and a *.override.yml under apps/ in a snapshot-restricted run and asserts they produce an observation. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 2b). Verified at head b2259fe03f of open pull request #2151; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
